audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Judges / Shoftim Danite land search, seizure of Micah's shrine and Levite, Laish destruction, and Dan shrine narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Dan's unsettled inheritance, five-person reconnaissance, Levite oracle, Laish's quiet and isolation, six-hundred-person armed migration, theft of shrine objects, clerical recruitment under armed pressure, Micah's protest, destruction of Laish, colonial renaming, Jonathan genealogy textual issue, and rival shrine chronology.

verses.restored: In those days there was no king in Israel. In those days tribe of Dan was seeking for itself an inheritance in which to dwell, because until that day an inheritance had not fallen to it among tribes of Israel.

familiar.text: In those days there was no king in Israel: and in those days the tribe of the Danites sought them an inheritance to dwell in; for unto that day all their inheritance had not fallen unto them among the tribes of Israel.

modern.text: In those days there was no king in Israel, and the tribe of the Danites was looking for territory to occupy. For up to that time they had not come into an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.

original.text: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם אֵ֥ין מֶ֖לֶךְ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּבַיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֗ם שֵׁ֣בֶט הַדָּנִ֞י מְבַקֶּשׁ ל֤וֹ נַֽחֲלָה֙ לָשֶׁ֔בֶת כִּי֩ לֹֽא נָ֨פְלָה לּ֜וֹ עַד הַיּ֥וֹם הַה֛וּא בְּתוֹךְ שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּנַחֲלָֽה

verses.restored: Children of Dan sent from their clan five men from their whole number, men of strength, from Zorah and Eshtaol, to spy out land and search it. They said to them, Go, search land. They came to hill country of Ephraim, to house of Micah, and lodged there.

familiar.text: And the children of Dan sent of their family five men from their coasts, men of valour, from Zorah, and from Eshtaol, to spy out the land, and to search it; and they said unto them, Go, search the land: who when they came to mount Ephraim, to the house of Micah, they lodged there.

modern.text: So the Danites sent out five men from their clans, men of valor from Zorah and Eshtaol, to spy out the land and explore it. “Go and explore the land,” they told them. The men entered the hill country of Ephraim and came to the house of Micah, where they spent the night.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלְח֣וּ בְנֵי דָ֣ן מִֽמִּשְׁפַּחְתָּ֡ם חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה אֲנָשִׁ֣ים מִקְצוֹתָם֩ אֲנָשִׁ֨ים בְּנֵי חַ֜יִל מִצָּרְעָ֣ה וּמֵֽאֶשְׁתָּאֹ֗ל לְרַגֵּ֤ל אֶת הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ וּלְחָקְרָ֔הּ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם לְכ֖וּ חִקְר֣וּ אֶת הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיָּבֹ֤אוּ הַר אֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ עַד בֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֔ה וַיָּלִ֖ינוּ שָֽׁם

verses.restored: When they were near house of Micah, they recognized voice of young Levite. They turned aside there and said to him, Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? What do you have here?

familiar.text: When they were by the house of Micah, they knew the voice of the young man the Levite: and they turned in thither, and said unto him, Who brought thee hither? and what makest thou in this place? and what hast thou here?

modern.text: And while they were near Micah’s house, they recognized the voice of the young Levite; so they went over and asked him, “Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? Why are you here?”

original.text: הֵ֚מָּה עִם בֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֔ה וְהֵ֣מָּה הִכִּ֔ירוּ אֶת ק֥וֹל הַנַּ֖עַר הַלֵּוִ֑י וַיָּס֣וּרוּ שָׁ֗ם וַיֹּ֤אמְרוּ לוֹ֙ מִֽי הֱבִיאֲךָ֣ הֲלֹ֔ם וּמָֽה אַתָּ֥ה עֹשֶׂ֛ה בָּזֶ֖ה וּמַה לְּךָ֥ פֹֽה

verses.restored: He said to them, Thus and thus Micah has done for me; he hired me, and I became his priest.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Thus and thus dealeth Micah with me, and hath hired me, and I am his priest.

modern.text: “Micah has done this and that for me,” he replied, “and he has hired me to be his priest.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם כָּזֹ֣ה וְכָזֶ֔ה עָ֥שָׂה לִ֖י מִיכָ֑ה וַיִּשְׂכְּרֵ֕נִי וָאֱהִי ל֖וֹ לְכֹהֵֽן

verses.restored: They said to him, Inquire, please, of Divine, so we may know whether our way upon which we are going will prosper.

familiar.text: And they said unto him, Ask counsel, we pray thee, of God, that we may know whether our way which we go shall be prosperous.

modern.text: Then they said to him, “Please inquire of God to determine whether we will have a successful journey.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמְרוּ ל֖וֹ שְׁאַל נָ֣א בֵאלֹהִ֑ים וְנֵ֣דְעָ֔ה הֲתַצְלִ֣יחַ דַּרְכֵּ֔נוּ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנַ֖חְנוּ הֹלְכִ֥ים עָלֶֽיהָ

verses.restored: The priest said to them, Go in peace. Before YHWH is your way upon which you are going.

familiar.text: And the priest said unto them, Go in peace: before the LORD is your way wherein ye go.

modern.text: And the priest told them, “Go in peace. The LORD is watching over your journey.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר לָהֶ֛ם הַכֹּהֵ֖ן לְכ֣וּ לְשָׁל֑וֹם נֹ֣כַח יְהוָ֔ה דַּרְכְּכֶ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר תֵּֽלְכוּ בָֽהּ

verses.restored: The five men went and came to Laish. They saw people who were within it dwelling securely, according to manner of Sidonians, quiet and unsuspecting, with no one in the land humiliating or dispossessing them in any matter. They were far from Sidonians and had no dealings with other people.

familiar.text: Then the five men departed, and came to Laish, and saw the people that were therein, how they dwelt careless, after the manner of the Zidonians, quiet and secure; and there was no magistrate in the land, that might put them to shame in any thing; and they were far from the Zidonians, and had no business with any man.

modern.text: So the five men departed and came to Laish, where they saw that the people were living securely, like the Sidonians, tranquil and unsuspecting. There was nothing lacking in the land and no oppressive ruler. And they were far away from the Sidonians and had no alliance with anyone.

original.text: וַיֵּלְכוּ֙ חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֔ים וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ לָ֑יְשָׁה וַיִּרְא֣וּ אֶת הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר בְּקִרְבָּ֣הּ יוֹשֶֽׁבֶת לָ֠בֶטַח כְּמִשְׁפַּ֨ט צִדֹנִ֜ים שֹׁקֵ֣ט וּבֹטֵ֗חַ וְאֵין מַכְלִ֨ים דָּבָ֤ר בָּאָ֨רֶץ֙ יוֹרֵ֣שׁ עֶ֔צֶר וּרְחֹקִ֥ים הֵ֨מָּה֙ מִצִּ֣דֹנִ֔ים וְדָבָ֥ר אֵין לָהֶ֖ם עִם אָדָֽם

verses.restored: They came to their brothers at Zorah and Eshtaol, and their brothers said to them, What do you report?

familiar.text: And they came unto their brethren to Zorah and Eshtaol: and their brethren said unto them, What say ye?

modern.text: When the men returned to Zorah and Eshtaol, their brothers asked them, “What did you find?”

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ אֶל אֲחֵיהֶ֔ם צָרְעָ֖ה וְאֶשְׁתָּאֹ֑ל וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ לָהֶ֛ם אֲחֵיהֶ֖ם מָ֥ה אַתֶּֽם

verses.restored: They said, Arise, and let us go up against them, because we have seen the land, and look, it is very good. Will you remain silent? Do not be slow to go, to enter, to possess the land.

familiar.text: And they said, Arise, that we may go up against them: for we have seen the land, and, behold, it is very good: and are ye still? be not slothful to go, and to enter to possess the land.

modern.text: They answered, “Come on, let us go up against them, for we have seen the land, and it is very good. Why would you fail to act? Do not hesitate to go there and take possession of the land!

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ ק֚וּמָה וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כִּ֤י רָאִ֨ינוּ֙ אֶת הָאָ֔רֶץ וְהִנֵּ֥ה טוֹבָ֖ה מְאֹ֑ד וְאַתֶּ֣ם מַחְשִׁ֔ים אַל תֵּעָ֣צְל֔וּ לָלֶ֥כֶת לָבֹ֖א לָרֶ֥שֶׁת אֶת הָאָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: When you go, you will come to an unsuspecting people and a broad land, because Divine has given it into your hand, a place where there is no lack of anything that is in the earth.

familiar.text: When ye go, ye shall come unto a people secure, and to a large land: for God hath given it into your hands; a place where there is no want of any thing that is in the earth.

modern.text: When you enter, you will come to an unsuspecting people and a spacious land, for God has delivered it into your hand. It is a place where nothing on earth is lacking.”

original.text: כְּבֹאֲכֶ֞ם תָּבֹ֣אוּ אֶל עַ֣ם בֹּטֵ֗חַ וְהָאָ֨רֶץ֙ רַחֲבַ֣ת יָדַ֔יִם כִּֽי נְתָנָ֥הּ אֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּיֶדְכֶ֑ם מָקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֵֽין שָׁ֣ם מַחְס֔וֹר כָּל דָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּאָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: Six hundred men from clan of Dan set out from Zorah and Eshtaol, equipped with weapons of war.

familiar.text: And there went from thence of the family of the Danites, out of Zorah and out of Eshtaol, six hundred men appointed with weapons of war.

modern.text: So six hundred Danites departed from Zorah and Eshtaol, armed with weapons of war.

original.text: וַיִּסְע֤וּ מִשָּׁם֙ מִמִּשְׁפַּ֣חַת הַדָּנִ֔י מִצָּרְעָ֖ה וּמֵאֶשְׁתָּאֹ֑ל שֵֽׁשׁ מֵא֣וֹת אִ֔ישׁ חָג֖וּר כְּלֵ֥י מִלְחָמָֽה

verses.restored: They went up and camped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah. Therefore they call that place Mahaneh-dan to this day; look, it is west of Kiriath-jearim.

familiar.text: And they went up, and pitched in Kirjathjearim, in Judah: wherefore they called that place Mahanehdan unto this day: behold, it is behind Kirjathjearim.

modern.text: They went up and camped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah. That is why the place west of Kiriath-jearim is called Mahaneh-dan to this day.

original.text: וַֽיַּעֲל֗וּ וַֽיַּחֲנ֛וּ בְּקִרְיַ֥ת יְעָרִ֖ים בִּֽיהוּדָ֑ה עַל כֵּ֡ן קָרְאוּ֩ לַמָּק֨וֹם הַה֜וּא מַחֲנֵה דָ֗ן עַ֚ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה הִנֵּ֕ה אַחֲרֵ֖י קִרְיַ֥ת יְעָרִֽים

verses.restored: They passed from there to hill country of Ephraim and came to house of Micah.

familiar.text: And they passed thence unto mount Ephraim, and came unto the house of Micah.

modern.text: And from there they traveled to the hill country of Ephraim and came to Micah’s house. The Danites Take Micah’s Idols

original.text: וַיַּעַבְר֥וּ מִשָּׁ֖ם הַר אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ עַד בֵּ֥ית מִיכָֽה

verses.restored: The five men who had gone to spy out land of Laish answered and said to their brothers, Do you know that in these houses are an ephod, teraphim, a carved image, and a cast image? Now know what you will do.

familiar.text: Then answered the five men that went to spy out the country of Laish, and said unto their brethren, Do ye know that there is in these houses an ephod, and teraphim, and a graven image, and a molten image? now therefore consider what ye have to do.

modern.text: Then the five men who had gone to spy out the land of Laish said to their brothers, “Did you know that one of these houses has an ephod, household gods, a graven image, and a molten idol? Now think about what you should do.”

original.text: וַֽיַּעֲנ֞וּ חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים הַהֹלְכִים֮ לְרַגֵּל֮ אֶת הָאָ֣רֶץ לַיִשׁ֒ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אֶל אֲחֵיהֶ֔ם הַיְדַעְתֶּ֗ם כִּ֠י יֵ֣שׁ בַּבָּתִּ֤ים הָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ אֵפ֣וֹד וּתְרָפִ֔ים וּפֶ֖סֶל וּמַסֵּכָ֑ה וְעַתָּ֖ה דְּע֥וּ מַֽה תַּעֲשֽׂוּ

verses.restored: They turned aside there, came to house of young Levite, house of Micah, and asked him concerning peace.

familiar.text: And they turned thitherward, and came to the house of the young man the Levite, even unto the house of Micah, and saluted him.

modern.text: So they turned aside there and went to the home of the young Levite, the house of Micah, and greeted him.

original.text: וַיָּס֣וּרוּ שָׁ֔מָּה וַיָּבֹ֛אוּ אֶל בֵּֽית הַנַּ֥עַר הַלֵּוִ֖י בֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁאֲלוּ ל֖וֹ לְשָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: The six hundred men from children of Dan, equipped with their weapons of war, stood at entrance of gate.

familiar.text: And the six hundred men appointed with their weapons of war, which were of the children of Dan, stood by the entering of the gate.

modern.text: The six hundred Danites stood at the entrance of the gate, armed with their weapons of war.

original.text: וְשֵׁשׁ מֵא֣וֹת אִ֗ישׁ חֲגוּרִים֙ כְּלֵ֣י מִלְחַמְתָּ֔ם נִצָּבִ֖ים פֶּ֣תַח הַשָּׁ֑עַר אֲשֶׁ֖ר מִבְּנֵי דָֽן

verses.restored: The five men who had gone to spy out land went up and entered there. They took carved image, ephod, teraphim, and cast image, while the priest stood at entrance of gate with the six hundred men equipped with weapons of war.

familiar.text: And the five men that went to spy out the land went up, and came in thither, and took the graven image, and the ephod, and the teraphim, and the molten image: and the priest stood in the entering of the gate with the six hundred men that were appointed with weapons of war.

modern.text: And the five men who had gone to spy out the land went inside and took the graven image, the ephod, the household idols, and the molten idol, while the priest stood at the entrance of the gate with the six hundred armed men.

original.text: וַֽיַּעֲל֞וּ חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים הַהֹלְכִים֮ לְרַגֵּ֣ל אֶת הָאָרֶץ֒ בָּ֣אוּ שָׁ֔מָּה לָקְח֗וּ אֶת הַפֶּ֨סֶל֙ וְאֶת הָ֣אֵפ֔וֹד וְאֶת הַתְּרָפִ֖ים וְאֶת הַמַּסֵּכָ֑ה וְהַכֹּהֵ֗ן נִצָּב֙ פֶּ֣תַח הַשַּׁ֔עַר וְשֵׁשׁ מֵא֣וֹת הָאִ֔ישׁ הֶחָג֖וּר כְּלֵ֥י הַמִּלְחָמָֽה

verses.restored: When these entered house of Micah and took carved image, ephod, teraphim, and cast image, the priest said to them, What are you doing?

familiar.text: And these went into Micah’s house, and fetched the carved image, the ephod, and the teraphim, and the molten image. Then said the priest unto them, What do ye?

modern.text: When they entered Micah’s house and took the graven image, the ephod, the household idols, and the molten idol, the priest said to them, “What are you doing?”

original.text: וְאֵ֗לֶּה בָּ֚אוּ בֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֔ה וַיִּקְחוּ֙ אֶת פֶּ֣סֶל הָאֵפ֔וֹד וְאֶת הַתְּרָפִ֖ים וְאֶת הַמַּסֵּכָ֑ה וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן מָ֥ה אַתֶּ֖ם עֹשִֽׂים

verses.restored: They said to him, Be silent; place your hand upon your mouth and go with us, and be to us a father and a priest. Is it better for you to be priest to house of one man or to be priest to a tribe and clan in Israel?

familiar.text: And they said unto him, Hold thy peace, lay thine hand upon thy mouth, and go with us, and be to us a father and a priest: is it better for thee to be a priest unto the house of one man, or that thou be a priest unto a tribe and a family in Israel?

modern.text: “Be quiet,” they told him. “Put your hand over your mouth and come with us and be a father and a priest to us. Is it better for you to be a priest for the house of one person or a priest for a tribe and family in Israel?”

original.text: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֩ ל֨וֹ הַחֲרֵ֜שׁ שִֽׂים יָדְךָ֤ עַל פִּ֨יךָ֙ וְלֵ֣ךְ עִמָּ֔נוּ וֶֽהְיֵה לָ֖נוּ לְאָ֣ב וּלְכֹהֵ֑ן הֲט֣וֹב הֱיוֹתְךָ֣ כֹהֵ֗ן לְבֵית֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֔ד א֚וֹ הֱיוֹתְךָ֣ כֹהֵ֔ן לְשֵׁ֥בֶט וּלְמִשְׁפָּחָ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Heart of the priest was glad. He took ephod, teraphim, and carved image and came into midst of people.

familiar.text: And the priest’s heart was glad, and he took the ephod, and the teraphim, and the graven image, and went in the midst of the people.

modern.text: So the priest was glad and took the ephod, the household idols, and the graven image, and went with the people.

original.text: וַיִּיטַב֙ לֵ֣ב הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וַיִּקַּח֙ אֶת הָ֣אֵפ֔וֹד וְאֶת הַתְּרָפִ֖ים וְאֶת הַפָּ֑סֶל וַיָּבֹ֖א בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָעָֽם

verses.restored: They turned and went, and put little ones, livestock, and valuable goods before them.

familiar.text: So they turned and departed, and put the little ones and the cattle and the carriage before them.

modern.text: Putting their small children, their livestock, and their possessions in front of them, they turned and departed.

original.text: וַיִּפְנ֖וּ וַיֵּלֵ֑כוּ וַיָּשִׂ֨ימוּ אֶת הַטַּ֧ף וְאֶת הַמִּקְנֶ֛ה וְאֶת הַכְּבוּדָּ֖ה לִפְנֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: When they had gone some distance from house of Micah, men who were in houses near house of Micah were called together and overtook children of Dan.

familiar.text: And when they were a good way from the house of Micah, the men that were in the houses near to Micah’s house were gathered together, and overtook the children of Dan.

modern.text: After they were some distance from Micah’s house, the men in the houses near Micah’s house mobilized and overtook the Danites.

original.text: הֵ֥מָּה הִרְחִ֖יקוּ מִבֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֑ה וְהָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר בַּבָּתִּים֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ עִם בֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֔ה נִֽזְעֲק֔וּ וַיַּדְבִּ֖יקוּ אֶת בְּנֵי דָֽן

verses.restored: They called to children of Dan. They turned their faces and said to Micah, What is wrong with you, that you have been called together?

familiar.text: And they cried unto the children of Dan. And they turned their faces, and said unto Micah, What aileth thee, that thou comest with such a company?

modern.text: When they called out after them, the Danites turned to face them and said to Micah, “What is the matter with you that you have called out such a company?”

original.text: וַֽיִּקְרְאוּ֙ אֶל בְּנֵי דָ֔ן וַיַּסֵּ֖בּוּ פְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לְמִיכָ֔ה מַה לְּךָ֖ כִּ֥י נִזְעָֽקְתָּ

verses.restored: He said, My gods that I made you have taken, and the priest, and you have gone away. What remains to me? How then can you say to me, What is wrong with you?

familiar.text: And he said, Ye have taken away my gods which I made, and the priest, and ye are gone away: and what have I more? and what is this that ye say unto me, What aileth thee?

modern.text: He replied, “You took the gods I had made, and my priest, and went away. What else do I have? How can you say to me, ‘What is the matter with you?’”

original.text: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר אֶת אֱלֹהַי֩ אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂ֨יתִי לְקַחְתֶּ֧ם וְֽאֶת הַכֹּהֵ֛ן וַתֵּלְכ֖וּ וּמַה לִּ֣י ע֑וֹד וּמַה זֶּ֛ה תֹּאמְר֥וּ אֵלַ֖י מַה לָּֽךְ

verses.restored: Children of Dan said to him, Do not let your voice be heard among us, lest men bitter of life strike you, and you gather up your life and life of your household.

familiar.text: And the children of Dan said unto him, Let not thy voice be heard among us, lest angry fellows run upon thee, and thou lose thy life, with the lives of thy household.

modern.text: The Danites said to him, “Do not raise your voice against us, or angry men will attack you, and you and your family will lose your lives.”

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ אֵלָיו֙ בְּנֵי דָ֔ן אַל תַּשְׁמַ֥ע קוֹלְךָ֖ עִמָּ֑נוּ פֶּֽן יִפְגְּע֣וּ בָכֶ֗ם אֲנָשִׁים֙ מָ֣רֵי נֶ֔פֶשׁ וְאָסַפְתָּ֥ה נַפְשְׁךָ֖ וְנֶ֥פֶשׁ בֵּיתֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Children of Dan went on their way. Micah saw that they were stronger than he, so he turned and went back to his house.

familiar.text: And the children of Dan went their way: and when Micah saw that they were too strong for him, he turned and went back unto his house.

modern.text: So the Danites went on their way, and Micah turned to go back home, because he saw that they were too strong for him.

original.text: וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ בְנֵי דָ֖ן לְדַרְכָּ֑ם וַיַּ֣רְא מִיכָ֗ה כִּי חֲזָקִ֥ים הֵ֨מָּה֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וַיִּ֖פֶן וַיָּ֥שָׁב אֶל בֵּיתֽוֹ

verses.restored: They took what Micah had made and the priest who had been his, and came upon Laish, upon a quiet and unsuspecting people. They struck them by edge of sword and burned city with fire.

familiar.text: And they took the things which Micah had made, and the priest which he had, and came unto Laish, unto a people that were at quiet and secure: and they smote them with the edge of the sword, and burnt the city with fire.

modern.text: After they had taken Micah’s idols and his priest, they went to Laish, to a tranquil and unsuspecting people, and they struck them with their swords and burned down the city.

original.text: וְהֵ֨מָּה לָקְח֜וּ אֵ֧ת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֣ה מִיכָ֗ה וְֽאֶת הַכֹּהֵן֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָה לוֹ֒ וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ עַל לַ֗יִשׁ עַל עַם֙ שֹׁקֵ֣ט וּבֹטֵ֔חַ וַיַּכּ֥וּ אוֹתָ֖ם לְפִי חָ֑רֶב וְאֶת הָעִ֖יר שָׂרְפ֥וּ בָאֵֽשׁ

verses.restored: There was no deliverer, because it was far from Sidon and they had no dealings with other people. It was in valley belonging to Beth-rehob. They built the city and dwelt in it.

familiar.text: And there was no deliverer, because it was far from Zidon, and they had no business with any man; and it was in the valley that lieth by Bethrehob. And they built a city, and dwelt therein.

modern.text: There was no one to deliver them, because the city was far from Sidon and had no alliance with anyone; it was in a valley near Beth-rehob. And the Danites rebuilt the city and lived there.

original.text: וְאֵ֨ין מַצִּ֜יל כִּ֧י רְֽחוֹקָה הִ֣יא מִצִּיד֗וֹן וְדָבָ֤ר אֵין לָהֶם֙ עִם אָדָ֔ם וְהִ֕יא בָּעֵ֖מֶק אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְבֵית רְח֑וֹב וַיִּבְנ֥וּ אֶת הָעִ֖יר וַיֵּ֥שְׁבוּ בָֽהּ

verses.restored: They called name of city Dan, after name of Dan their father who was born to Israel; but Laish was name of city at first.

familiar.text: And they called the name of the city Dan, after the name of Dan their father, who was born unto Israel: howbeit the name of the city was Laish at the first.

modern.text: They named it Dan, after their forefather Dan, who was born to Israel—though the city was formerly named Laish.

original.text: וַיִּקְרְא֤וּ שֵׁם הָעִיר֙ דָּ֔ן בְּשֵׁם֙ דָּ֣ן אֲבִיהֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יוּלַּ֖ד לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְאוּלָ֛ם לַ֥יִשׁ שֵׁם הָעִ֖יר לָרִאשֹׁנָֽה

verses.restored: Children of Dan set up for themselves the carved image. Jonathan son of Gershom son of Manasseh/Moses, he and his sons were priests to tribe of Dan until day of captivity of land.

familiar.text: And the children of Dan set up the graven image: and Jonathan, the son of Gershom, the son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land.

modern.text: The Danites set up idols for themselves, and Jonathan son of Gershom, the son of Moses, and his sons were priests for the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land.

original.text: וַיָּקִ֧ימוּ לָהֶ֛ם בְּנֵי דָ֖ן אֶת הַפָּ֑סֶל וִ֠יהוֹנָתָן בֶּן גֵּרְשֹׁ֨ם בֶּן מְנַשֶּׁ֜ה ה֣וּא וּבָנָ֗יו הָי֤וּ כֹהֲנִים֙ לְשֵׁ֣בֶט הַדָּנִ֔י עַד י֖וֹם גְּל֥וֹת הָאָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: They set up for themselves carved image of Micah that he had made, all days that house of Divine was at Shiloh.

familiar.text: And they set them up Micah’s graven image, which he made, all the time that the house of God was in Shiloh.

modern.text: So they set up for themselves Micah’s graven image, and it was there the whole time the house of God was in Shiloh.

original.text: וַיָּשִׂ֣ימוּ לָהֶ֔ם אֶת פֶּ֥סֶל מִיכָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה כָּל יְמֵ֛י הֱי֥וֹת בֵּית הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּשִׁלֹֽה

translation_notes: Dan's lack of secure territory is a real condition of displacement, but the narrative's response is not ethically innocent: scouts identify an isolated, peaceful population precisely because it can be attacked without rescue.

Verse 7 is textually difficult. Its central picture is clear: Laish is quiet, unsuspecting, distant from allies, and not expecting dispossession. Those conditions increase vulnerability; they do not create moral permission for conquest.

The Levite's oracle that their way is before YHWH is reported inside a compromised shrine economy. It must not be treated as Divine endorsement of theft, forced migration, colonial seizure, or massacre.

The six hundred armed men surround the priest while shrine objects are taken. His later gladness and career advancement occur within an armed takeover; the scene should not be simplified into fully free vocational choice.
The command to put a hand over the mouth is coercive silencing. Religious workers may not be pressured into changing allegiance by threats, prestige, or institutional scale.

Micah's claim, 'my gods that I made,' exposes his possessive religious logic, but Dan's superior force does not make their theft just. Critique of Micah's shrine cannot become permission for religious persecution or cultural plunder.

Laish is attacked as a quiet civilian settlement, burned, rebuilt, and renamed. This is colonial conquest and population destruction, not an uplifting model of claiming promise or finding one's place.

Jonathan's ancestry is textually sensitive. The Masoretic tradition visually inserts a suspended nun in 'Manasseh,' while many scholars understand an original 'Moses.' Later audit must preserve the witness history without anti-Moses polemic.

The Dan shrine is contrasted chronologically with the house of Divine at Shiloh. The text preserves a rivalry of sanctuaries; it must not be weaponized into antisemitism, supersessionism, or attacks on present-day worship communities.
safety_note: Maximum anti-colonial and anti-xenophobia safeguards: Laish's isolation, peace, wealth, or lack of military alliance never makes its people disposable. Do not glamorize armed reconnaissance, seizure of sacred objects, coerced clergy, civilian massacre, city burning, territorial replacement, or renaming conquered land. Do not turn this chapter into permission for modern ethnic cleansing, settler violence, religious theft, or claims that prosperity proves Divine authorization.
